questions.question: Which smaller units are linked to form proteins?
choices: Amino acids
Monosaccharides
Fatty acids only
Nucleotides

questions.question: Which molecule stores hereditary information in most cells?
choices: Starch
DNA
Triglyceride
Cellulose

questions.question: Which biological molecule group includes starch and glycogen?
choices: Proteins
Nucleic acids
Carbohydrates
Steroids

questions.question: Which molecule group includes fats and phospholipids?
choices: Nucleic acids
Polypeptides
Simple sugars
Lipids

questions.question: What is the active site of an enzyme?
choices: The region where a substrate binds and the reaction occurs
The region containing an entire chromosome
A storage site for all cell waste
A channel through every cell wall

questions.question: What is a substrate in an enzyme-controlled reaction?
choices: The final product of every reaction
A reactant acted on by the enzyme
A gene coding for the enzyme
The temperature at which the enzyme stops

questions.question: What is an enzyme cofactor?
choices: The substrate that every enzyme turns into its product
The gene that carries every enzyme's amino-acid sequence
A nonprotein helper required for some enzymes to function
The final product of any enzyme-controlled reaction

questions.question: How does an enzyme increase reaction rate?
choices: It raises the energy of every product permanently
It changes the reaction's equilibrium to products only
It is consumed as the main energy source each time
It lowers the activation energy

questions.question: Why can very high temperatures reduce enzyme activity?
choices: They can disrupt the enzyme's functional shape
They always increase activity without an upper limit
They increase activity by enlarging every active site
They permanently increase enzyme concentration

questions.question: Why can an enzyme work on one substrate but not another?
choices: Every substrate binds with the same strength
Binding depends on compatible shape and chemical properties
Binding depends only on the substrate's mass
Only the enzyme's concentration determines which substrate binds

questions.question: How does hydrolysis help break down biological polymers?
choices: Smaller units join while water is removed
Water changes the order of atoms without breaking bonds
Water participates in breaking bonds between smaller units
Water moves the intact polymer across a membrane

questions.question: What generally happens to an enzyme after it releases its products?
choices: It becomes the main product permanently
It loses all of its atoms
It turns into a nucleotide
It can catalyze another reaction

questions.question: Why do phospholipids form bilayers in water?
choices: Their water-attracting heads face water while tails cluster away from it
Their heads and tails dissolve equally in water
They have no electrically uneven regions
They become solid mineral crystals

questions.question: Why can a pH change alter enzyme activity?
choices: It alters only the amount of substrate, never the enzyme
It can change charges and interactions important to the active site
It changes temperature without affecting molecular interactions
It makes every enzyme work equally well at any pH

questions.question: Why is ATP useful in cells?
choices: It stores an organism's complete hereditary code
It replaces every enzyme
Its reactions can be coupled to energy-requiring processes
It makes energy conservation unnecessary

questions.question: With enzyme amount fixed, adding substrate raises the rate at first but eventually has little effect. Why?
choices: The substrates lose all their chemical bonds before binding
The enzyme starts producing new elements
The reaction no longer needs reactants
The available active sites become occupied most of the time

questions.question: An inhibitor competes with a substrate for the active site. Which change can often reduce its effect?
choices: Increasing substrate concentration
Removing every substrate molecule
Destroying all enzyme proteins
Reducing the amount of enzyme to zero

questions.question: An enzyme works best at pH 7 and poorly at pH 3. What is the best conclusion?
choices: All enzymes work best at pH 7
Its activity depends on the chemical conditions
The enzyme has no active site
The substrate becomes a different element at pH 3

questions.question: A protein is heated until it loses its normal shape but its amino-acid sequence remains largely intact. What has occurred?
choices: DNA replication
Photosynthesis
Denaturation
Nuclear fission

questions.question: An enzyme speeds both directions of a reversible reaction. What happens to its equilibrium position at unchanged temperature?
choices: It shifts entirely to the products
It shifts entirely to the reactants
It becomes independent of concentrations
It remains unchanged, though equilibrium is reached sooner
